done_when: Find which one it is: if Forge can return before the app-server process exits, make it wait for the exit; if it's only the check, make the test tell a leftover process from a reused PID. test_4_turn_log passes on Windows CI three runs in a row

findings.body: If a process query fails after the initial live-process check, empty stdout becomes `None`, so `_left(recorded_server)` returns false and the leak assertion passes even when the app-server remains alive. Partial output can likewise produce a nonmatching identity. The Windows script also lacks `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, allowing query errors to reach `exit 3`. Production distinguishes absent processes from failed queries in `src/forge/codex.py:310–324`, and `tests/test_codex_record.py:267–269` covers that distinction. Validate query status and complete identity fields, fail on unexpected errors, and return `None` only for confirmed absence.
findings.title: Reject failed identity queries instead of treating them as process exit

why: tests/test_codex_worker.py::test_4_turn_log fails on Windows CI about one run in two: right after forge work returns, tasklist still lists one of the four reported Codex app-server PIDs (either Forge returns before the process has fully exited on Windows, or Windows reused the PID)
